content.thinking:
I need to plan the design carefully before writing the full file in one pass. I'm thinking through the character concept—a humanoid cyborg medic in an Overwatch-inspired style, around 1.75m tall, with a white/cream armor color scheme over a dark graphite undersuit and a single strong accent color, possibly teal or orange, for the medical glow details.

Now I'm working out the cyborg details: an exposed mechanical left arm with glowing graphite components, a half face plate, and a healing staff with a glowing ring core planted on the floor near the right hand. I'm also sketching the skeleton structure—hips, spine chain, neck, head, jaw, arms, legs, and simplified finger chains—aiming for a readable A-pose with arms angled down about 35 degrees, positioning the shoulder, elbow, and hand coordinates so the staff sits naturally planted beside the gripping hand.

I'm figuring out staff length and placement so it spans from the floor to roughly head height while being held mid-shaft, then planning which helper API functions (parts, sweeps, rods, lofts, joints, chains) I'll need to build the figure, leaning toward a clean Overwatch-style flat-color palette with selective gradient paints for panel highlights rather than heavy cel shading.

I'm limiting myself to around 14 flat colors plus a few panel-line paints to stay well under the color budget. I'm also sorting out coordinate conventions (left is +X, model-space positions for parts, explicit bone assignment for limbs) and starting to lay out the skeleton hierarchy beginning with the hips as the root joint.

Working through the spine chain, deciding how many joints to use between hips and chest and how to name them so the chain's path points and tip joint line up correctly.

Then I'll build the neck chain from the top of the spine to a head joint, and add a jaw joint parented to the head for the mouth movement.

Let me finalize: chin at 1.55, head center 1.66, top ~1.78, with a short neck segment from spine end up to head base, shoulders around y1.32. Going for a slightly stylized heroic proportion, head roughly 1/7 of total height.

For the legs, I'm setting hip joints near x=±0.095, y≈0.92-0.93, using a two-bone IK chain (thigh and shin around 0.43 each) with a forward-facing knee hint, targeting ankle height ~0.09-0.10 so the leg has a slight natural bend rather than being perfectly straight.

For the feet, I'm defining the ankle as the tip of the leg chain, then adding a separate toe joint parented to that ankle to create the foot's digit segment.

The leg chain parents to the hips, and I'm using a sign convention where s=1 is left (+X) with "L"/"R" suffixes on names. For the arms, I'm figuring out shoulder placement relative to the spine chain, parenting the shoulder to the third spine joint positioned partway up the torso.

I'm adding a clavicle joint between the spine and shoulder that aims toward the shoulder, then working out the A-pose arm angles — tilting the upper arm about 22° from vertical with slight forward offset, and computing the direction vectors for the upper arm segment before moving to the elbow.

Continuing the arm chain, I'm computing the elbow position from the shoulder, then the forearm direction with a slight forward bend to find the wrist location, and adding hand length to get the hand center. For the right arm, I need to adjust the wrist and hand position so the grip aligns with where the staff should sit vertically on that side of the body.

Computing symmetric wrist target for the other arm, then finding the hand grip center along the arm's direction vector offset from the wrist.

Now I'm positioning the staff vertically near the body, checking clearance against the leg and arm so nothing collides, then planning the hands: the left relaxed open and the right gripping, with fingers built as small capsule chains curling around the staff.

Budgeting joint counts across hips, spine, neck, head, arms, legs, and fingers to stay under the 160 limit, aiming for roughly 60 total with 10 joints per hand (four fingers plus thumb). I'm keeping finger geometry simple—straight slightly-curled paths for the left hand, and arcs wrapping the staff for the right hand's grip.

Still shaping the hand geometry...

I'll simplify and just pick concrete coordinates for the palm block and wrist position relative to the staff, rather than overanalyzing the exact grip anatomy.

Setting finger y-spacing at 0.022 intervals, and planning to rig each finger as a chain of joints along a polyline path with rounded corners, using five knot points mapped to four named segments per finger.

For the thumb, I'm positioning it to wrap opposite the fingers, placing its two-span chain slightly above and outside the index finger so it doesn't overlap, adjusting y and z coordinates to get a natural wrap over the top of the hand.

Now I'm working out the left hand, which hangs open with fingers pointing downward along the forearm's direction. I'm computing the palm center from the wrist position plus the forearm vector, then setting up the finger base points using a lateral offset perpendicular to that direction to space the fingers across the palm width.

For the right arm I'm sketching a robotic cyborg design with exposed dark metal plating and glowing teal strips, paired with a white armor pauldron, while the left arm stays a plain gauntlet sleeve; the face gets a glowing cyborg half-plate contrasted with natural hair pulled into a ponytail. I'm settling on a palette of whites, graphites, and steel tones for the armor pieces.

I'm locking in a bright teal-cyan glow as the single strong accent color, keeping everything else neutral (white, graphite, steel), and choosing auburn hair with warm skin tones and muted lip color, plus a small medical cross decal using the accent hue for a subtle healer motif.

For the armor's beveled edges, I'm weighing RoundedBoxGeometry from three's addons versus building panels with extrude geometry and bevels — the extrude approach feels safer for compatibility, so I'll lean toward that for the plates.

RoundedBoxGeometry has been available since r1xx, so it should be fine to use. I'm a bit uncertain whether the bundler maps "three/addons/..." imports to the same shared three copy as plain "three" imports, which could risk a duplicate module instance, but I'll proceed anyway.

To stay under the part count limit, I plan to merge geometries sharing the same bone and color using a batching helper that bakes transforms into each geometry before merging, since box, sphere, cylinder, and rounded box geometries all share compatible indexed attributes for merging.

For surface details I'm thinking through SVG decal textures — a chest emblem with a plus sign in a hexagon rather than anything resembling a logo, plus simple eye decals with sclera and iris shapes for the face.

I'm working out how decal placement works relative to a part's local frame, using directional words like forward/left/up that stay fixed to the model's own orientation regardless of how it's rotated in the world.

For the head itself, I'm planning a scaled sphere for the cranium plus a separate lower jaw piece attached at the jaw joint, keeping the mouth closed and painting lips rather than modeling teeth, and figuring out how surfaces work on a scaled sphere for decal placement.

Now I'm adding facial features like a small nose wedge, dark brow rods, lip capsule, and ears, plus designing the cyborg half-face: a human eye on the right, a glowing teal cybernetic lens on the left, and a curved steel plate covering the left cheek and eye socket using a partial sphere geometry since true clipping isn't possible.

Keeping that for now. For hair, I'm planning an auburn cap made from a scaled partial sphere over the upper back of the head, with bangs as extruded swoosh shapes and a ponytail built from a short joint chain trailing from the back of the skull.

I'm also adding a cyborg earpiece ring over the left ear with a small glowing antenna, then moving on to the torso — building the chest and undersuit as a loft along the spine, with a white armor plate layered over a dark bodysuit, working out how the cross-section widths and normals align along the vertical path.

Defining torso stations...

For the pelvis, I'll use a rounded box bound to the hips bone. For legs, I need a helper that places boxes along a bone segment, aiming them with the limb direction while keeping width along world X for proper orientation.

Setting up imports and boilerplate...

I'm setting metadata and figuring out texture resolution, estimating texel density for painted limb and torso surfaces to decide on paint size, then starting to define the skeleton structure.

Writing hips and spine chain...

Setting head centre, then placing the jaw hinge joint angled toward the chin, and starting on the clavicle joints attaching under spine3 near the shoulder base.

I'm now building the arm limb chain from shoulder through elbow to wrist as a point array, then attaching that chain to the clavicle, reasoning through whether a straight polyline or catmull-spline best represents the elbow bend given the sweep fillets will smooth the joint anyway.

The wrist becomes the arm's tip for attaching hands and fingers, and I'm sketching the leg limb similarly — computing hip-to-ankle reach so the knee bends forward correctly, then setting up the leg chain names and parenting it to the hips with a foot contact point.

I'm defining the toe joint off the ankle tip, keeping the boot's sole flush with y=0 so it matches floor contact without clipping, then setting up a reusable rounded-box geometry helper for building the body parts.

Now I'm sketching a `place` helper that wraps part creation with bone, position, and options, plus a `plate` helper for building segments that interpolates between two anchor points with configurable width, depth, and growth factor.

I'll import the Fill type from the context module for typing color inputs, then start planning the torso construction: an undersuit core as a graphite loft, with white chest armor plates layered on top.

For the chest armor, I'm sizing a loft that sits slightly larger than the undersuit at each cross-section so it visibly covers it, keeping all stations proportioned and increasing the sides count to 12 for smoother body curves.

Rather than overcomplicating things, I'll keep two separate lofts—graphite undersuit and white chest armor—and add a front emblem via a decal projected onto the chest surface at the correct z-depth, positioned centrally on the chest plate.

For the waist belt, I'll sweep a thin closed loop around the torso at a height within the torso loft's valid range (y=1.03), confirming the plane intersects the surface properly so the decal/sweep doesn't throw errors.

Now I'm sketching the pelvis and hip armor: tasset plates as rounded boxes hanging at the hips, and I'm checking the torso loft's bottom station aligns with where the legs/thighs begin so there's no gap at the crotch.

I need to work out bone ownership along the spine chain near the hips—since hips and spine1 joints sit close together (0.95 vs 0.98), the blend span between them is narrow, so I'm deciding that hips should own the lower pelvis region (0.88–0.98) rather than spine1, keeping that motion tied to the hip bone.

Now I'm defining the spine chain path with points moving upward through spine1, spine2, and spine3, with the bone list grouping hips and spine as a unit. For the neck, I'm sweeping a tapered radius skin shape and adding a collar ring at the neck base, matching an Overwatch medic-style high collar.

I'm planning the arm sweeps next: a 3-joint chain (shoulder, elbow, wrist, plus tip) with tapering radii from shoulder down to wrist. The right arm gets a graphite undersuit sleeve on the upper arm with a white bracer on the forearm, while the left arm will be robotic.

Right arm plating: adding white armour plates covering the shoulder-elbow segment and a bracer plate on the forearm, plus a glove at the wrist. For the cyborg left arm, I'm switching to a segmented mech design instead—a dark metal upper-arm sweep with joint rings, exposed piston rods, and glowing teal conduit details along the surface.

White pauldrons get domed hemisphere shoulder armour with trim rings, bigger on the left side with a teal stripe accent, plus a mech forearm built from hexagonal frustum sections and a segmented mech hand with glowing teal fingertips. Legs will use a graphite undersuit sweep from thigh to shin.

Still designing leg armor...

Hands reuse the earlier part-chain approach. Now I'm moving to the staff design: a tall steel-white shaft topped with a glowing halo ring and teal core sphere for the healing staff.

I'm deciding to attach the staff as its own joint parented to the right wrist, positioned so its base rests at floor level, without needing a hinge role since it's a rigid held object.

Now I'm sketching the staff's geometry: a slender steel shaft with a wrapped grip section bounded by lathed collar rings, a cone-capped graphite foot with a glowing teal ring near the base, accent glow bands partway up the shaft, and a torus-shaped ring forming the head.

For the top ornament, I'm settling on a shaft height around 1.56 with an open crescent of curved prongs sweeping upward to cradle a glowing teal orb near y 1.69, with the prongs reaching toward 1.80 so the total staff height lands around 1.82 -- slightly taller than the character's head, which feels right for a support-hero staff.

I'm layering a front-facing ring around the orb plus a thinner perpendicular torus for a crosshair effect, with small glowing octahedron accents orbiting the orb and a pair of fan-shaped wing fins near y 1.5 flaring outward from the shaft for visual flair. I'll skip any text decals and keep the grip simple, maybe adding a small glowing power-cell window partway down the shaft for detail.

Now I'm working out the right hand placement: fitting the palm box and gripping fingers so the staff passes cleanly through the palm without clipping, adjusting the palm's depth and center so the staff's back edge just touches it, and aligning the wrist/forearm junction, finger curl, and thumb position so the whole grip looks anatomically coherent around the staff.

Checking the gap between fingers and staff, I see the radius is a bit loose, so I'll tighten the finger path to wrap around the staff at radius 0.03, centered on the staff axis.

Checking that the finger ring radius of .041 outer and .019 inner closes around the staff radius .0165, confirming contact on both sides. I'm setting up each hand's four finger chains with five joints apiece, spaced at y=.795 down to .729, each as its own separate sweep.

For the fingers I'm reducing to 4 points with 3 catmull spans spaced at -150,-50,50,150 degrees for a rounder ring instead of a plain polyline hexagon. For the left cyborg hand I'm computing a relaxed hanging pose from the wrist-to-elbow direction, placing the palm center along that vector and orienting the palm box to face inward toward the body.

Working out finger base offsets...

I'm sketching the steel finger chains for the cyborg hand with tapered sweeps and glowing fingertip spheres attached at the last joint, while planning the right hand's glove as graphite with teal cuffs and white knuckle highlights. For the face, I'm considering painted decals for eyebrows and lips rather than geometry.

Now I'm working out head geometry: skull sphere dimensions and position, a separate lower jaw part sized and placed so its front surface aligns with the skull's face plane, plus eye decals with a stylized teal iris on the right and a glowing cybernetic lens on the left, along with a half face plate housing electronics.

Decal targets only the skull, not the jaw. For the left cybernetic eye, I'm designing a glowing teal lens with a dark socket ring instead of a flat decal, built with a small cylinder shape for the plate covering that side of the face.

Working out disc placement...

Checking theta range for the plate covers brow to cheek, confirming the eye falls within bounds, and nudging the plate's edge slightly off-center so the nose bridge stays uncovered. I'm also deciding to skip rim sweeps and just scale the shell slightly larger to avoid thin visible gaps at the open edges.

Now I'm tightening that gap further, shrinking the shell scale to 3.5mm offset instead of 5mm for a tighter fit against the skull. Then I'm moving on to the hair cap geometry, realizing a full equatorial cap would cover the face entirely, so I need to constrain its phi range to leave a proper hairline at the forehead.

To fix the hairline, I'm trying tilting the hair cap backward by rotating it around the X axis rather than cutting its phi range — rotating by roughly -28° so the front rim rises to the forehead while the back rim drops toward the nape, giving a natural hairline shape.

For color, I'm thinking of using a countershading paint technique where hair facing upward gets a lighter highlight tone, mimicking a hand-painted gradient look across the ponytail and side locks.

Applying the same countershading trick to white armour gives a soft painted gradient—brighter on top, cooler shaded tones below, matching Overwatch's hand-painted material style. I need to bump the paint texture resolution since many painted parts share one material sheet, and I'm checking whether merged decor still evaluates correctly on baked positions.

Painting every surface at once will spread coverage thin, so I'm estimating texel density across the total armour and suit area to confirm 2048px resolution stays sharp enough, then setting up the builder with that paint size and a 4096 atlas. I'm also deciding which parts get painted gradients versus flat colours—armour, suit, skin, and hair with subtle shading, metals kept simple—while capping the overall palette to roughly 20 flat colours. Now I'm sketching a custom paint function to add thin horizontal panel-line grooves onto the white armour.

Defining color palettes...

Now I'm thinking through anatomical details - adding a medic pouch with a teal cross decal, a shoulder strap, glowing canister vials at the thigh, and a sleek medic backpack with vertical vents, drawing inspiration from Mercy's tech-wing silhouette.

Designing the back medical module...

Still writing transform logic...

I realize octahedron and other polyhedron geometries come out non-indexed, which breaks mergeGeometries if mixed with indexed ones, so I'll just always call toNonIndexed() on everything before merging to keep attributes consistent across the bundle.

For shading, calling computeVertexNormals() after converting to non-indexed gives automatic flat faceting for faceted parts, while smooth geometries like spheres can keep their original per-vertex normals untouched — so I don't need a separate flat-shading flag, just leave normals as-is unless I explicitly recompute them.

I'm thinking through texture painting next: since the merged geometry shares one material and paint map, I just need consistent UVs across pieces. Then I'll start defining helper functions and the skeleton setup for the builder, including joints and spine chain positions.

Writing skeleton setup code...

Defining per-side data...

Checking the chain API for arm and leg setup — passing point arrays directly should work with the expected types, and the contact option exists on chain options. I'll grab the wrist joint from the arm's tip with a non-null assertion since it's typed as possibly null, then move on to writing out the actual geometry.

Now I'm sketching the torso loft, stacking cross-sections at various heights with changing width and depth to shape the waist and chest, using the hips-to-spine bone with a rounded 12-sided profile. I need to watch out for the default round end caps — they'll bulge the silhouette below the hips and above the shoulders more than I want, so I may need to flatten those caps.

I'm defining the chest armor as a separate white loft layered just outside the undersuit's torso profile, slightly wider and deeper at each matching height to sit properly over it.

I still need to add a trim ring at the waist transition, build out hip skirt plates, and plan a glowing teal chest strip or emblem decal down the center.

For the chest emblem, I'm projecting a decal onto the front of the chest tube using a transparent texture showing a medical cross inside a hexagon with panel lines, teal glowing cross and darker trim, since decals return parts that can themselves glow.

I'm also thinking about a graphite rib-plate detail on the torso sides, and sketching a lathe profile for a collar ring at the neck base — defining a closed polygon of radius/height points to form the collar shape, then checking it fits against the wider trapezius slope of the chest armor's top edge.

Then I move to the neck collar itself: a lathe shape for the standing suit collar, plus a thin teal glow ring at the top rendered as a small torus for the rim light. I note the backpack should attach relative to the chest/spine bone, and I'm about to start on the pelvis and hip plates next.

Now I'm working out the belt — a sweep loop around the torso at y=1.02 with a defined radius and color, making sure it only cuts the torso surface and inherits blended skin weights from hips and spine. Then I place a belt buckle box with a glowing teal dot centered slightly in front of the torso, calculating its z-offset based on torso radius plus belt thickness.

Next I'm positioning hip armor plates on either side at the hips bone, checking they align with the torso's width at that height without clipping the thigh cylinders, then adding front tasset skirt plates that hang from the hips with a slight outward tilt so they clear the thigh geometry.

For the legs, I'm building each thigh as a tapered sweep chain from hip to knee using the suit color, verifying the top radius stays within the torso silhouette. Then I'm adding thigh armor plates positioned along the front of each thigh using lerp points between hip and knee, offset forward along the depth axis to sit just outside the leg surface.

I'm adding a side guard strip and a teal accent rod running along the outer thigh, plus a knee guard made from a scaled ellipsoid sphere with a small teal trim disc at the joint.

Now I'm working out the shin greave: positioning a plate from knee to ankle, computing forward offset by rotating the local z-axis offset using the bone's quaternion since the downward bone's local +Z maps to forward.

Confirming the cross product gives the correct perpendicular-forward vector: front = (0, dz, -dy) normalized, matching the projected forward direction in the yz plane. I'll use this to implement the plate helper with an offset parameter along that local z-axis.

Now I'm designing the plate function signature, taking endpoints, width, depth, offset, bone, and color plus optional fractions along the segment and a side offset, computing interpolated start/end points, the direction vector, and the perpendicular frame vector, handling the near-vertical edge case where the direction is mostly along y.

Now moving to the right arm, I'm defining a tapered sweep of radii from shoulder to wrist with an elbow bend at the midpoint, and adding a white pauldron shoulder piece using a scaled hemisphere shape.

I'm working out the rotation math so the pauldron tilts outward correctly on each side, then building it as a layered dome with a lip band and teal trim via a lathe profile.

Still refining the lathe profile points...

I'm planning the pauldrons: attaching to the shoulder joint, with the right one white with teal trim and the left cyborg-side one bigger and asymmetric with an exposed teal glow slit and graphite plating, reusing the same lathe function with scale and color parameters. Then adding a white upper-arm plate band.

For the right arm I'm adding a white bicep plate and a wrist bracer with teal trim rings. For the left cyborg arm I'm building a steel shoulder socket sphere and constructing the upper arm and forearm as rigid capsule/rod segments connecting shoulder to elbow with dark steel coloring and ring details.

Now I'm detailing the cyborg arm further: a graphite conduit core with steel segment rings and plates on the upper arm, plus thin piston rods with a teal glow band, and an armored hex forearm with white plates and teal glow strips leading to the mechanical hand. I'm also placing an elbow joint sphere with a teal glowing torus ring, and considering how to sweep teal healing-glow lines along the forearm surface.

Moving on, I'm laying out the hands (palm, knuckle plate, fingers, thumb on the right; palm and fingers on the left) and the staff, parenting it to the right wrist with specific x/z offsets, checking it clears the leg and hip plate. I'm also building the head details—ear, headset, hair, bangs—and defining a ponytail chain using a catmull spline through five points to create four named ponytail segments, then checking whether the hanging tail collides with the backpack position.

I'm adjusting the backpack height and shortening the ponytail's last point to avoid overlap, then sweeping the tail geometry with a tapering elliptical cross-section function and typing its return as a number tuple. I'm also adding a small cylindrical hair-tie ring at the ponytail base in a teal color.

For the bangs, I'm considering a swept fringe shape in the front view near the forehead, but deciding it's simpler to build a tilted hair cap angled back toward the hairline instead.

Working out the cap's tilt angle so the front rim sits just above the hairline, landing around y=1.705 once the extra elevation from tilting is factored in.

That gives hairline at 1.74, good. But checking the side rim elevation, it drops to about y=1.655, right where the ears sit at .095 radius, so the hair cap radius of .098 would partially cover the ears -- I should adjust the ear geometry to account for that overlap.

Positioning ears to protrude slightly beyond the cap with the headset covering the left one, leaving the right visible. Now adjusting the hair cap geometry's theta length and scale to fit snugly over the head.

I'm checking the hair cap's dimensions against the skull to confirm full coverage despite the backward shift and tilt, making sure the forehead area isn't exposed. I'm also considering adding side-swept bangs as a tube swept along a bezier path across the hairline from the temple.

Still writing hair locks...

Then I'll add a cyborg earpiece on the left ear with a steel disc and glow ring, plus separate eyebrow shapes for each side of the face.

Since the plate covers part of the left brow, I'll skip that one and instead add a steel ridge onto the plate itself for the right side.

For the nose, I'm considering a small cone shape angled forward and down into the face, keeping it simple without nostrils, then moving into shaping the lips as rounded rod pieces for the upper lip.

I need to figure out exactly where the mouth sits relative to the skull and jaw geometry -- since the jaw is a separate moving part, I'm placing the lower lip on the jaw surface and the upper lip on the fixed skull, calculating the z-depth at each y-position using the sphere equations for both head and jaw to make sure they align naturally when the mouth is closed.

Still calculating facial curve depths...

Mapping out the lip curve along the ellipsoid surface, computing z-values at several x points to get a slight dip-and-rise shape, then sweeping a thin capsule through those points with a rounded cap for the upper lip, with the lower lip positioned slightly below at the jaw line.

For the jaw, I'm computing similar radius falloff to get its front profile, deciding the jaw-to-upper-lip offset is small enough to skip a separate dark mouth line between them. For the eyes, I'm placing decals on the skull surface at the right height and depth, sizing them appropriately, and sketching out the eye graphic itself with an almond white shape, teal iris, pupil, and highlight details.

Since the cybernetic plate covers the left eye and hides any decal beneath it, I only need a plain decal for the right eye, giving it a human teal-green iris. I'm also working out the mirroring and orientation so the lash flick lands on the correct side given that the model's right eye appears on the viewer's left when facing it.

For the cybernetic eye on the plate, I'm placing a dark socket ring, a teal glowing lens disc, a small highlight sphere, and a thin scanline, calculating the exact z-depth so they sit flush against the curved shell surface without clipping.

Checking the plate's edge near the ear — at phi .85π the z-offset lands around .126, just before the ear position so the earpiece sits outside the plate boundary, which looks right. The cyborg plate covers the lower cheek and cheekbone while leaving the mouth area untouched, and its front edge near the nose comes out to roughly x≈.009, which seems like a reasonable boundary.

Now I'm working out the geometry for small teal glow rods running along the plate's surface, computing ellipsoid z-values at different x positions to make sure the rods trace the curved surface correctly from the eye toward the ear.

Still placing head details...

Now I'm planning the mirrored right ear, neck chain geometry, and a possible cyborg neck plate with glowing sockets. I'm also sketching out SVG textures for the eyes and a chest emblem, a teal cross on white armor with outline and chevrons.

Decal plan: glowing teal medic cross for chest, back pack decal with cross lines, hazard-style arm panel stripes, and a circuit decal for the cyborg arm — four textures total (eye, chest emblem, circuit, grille), with viewBox and stroke widths tuned for crisp rendering at different raster sizes, applied via decal calls onto the torso sweep. Now I'm starting to write out each body part definition in order.

Setting up imports...

Now I'm defining the color palette: teal accents for the glow, graphite and steel tones for the body, and skin/lip/brow shades for facial details.

Still writing geometry transform helper...

Writing the flush function...

I'm confirming part placement works without orientation since geometry origin maps to position, and that normals stay smooth after conversion. Now I'm sketching helper functions for common geometries like boxes, cylinders, and spheres, plus a non-merged part helper.

Writing part helper function...

Now I'm planning the SVG texture definitions, starting with an eye shape using an almond-like path, while keeping the overall content around 700 lines and double-checking API usage as I go.

Still writing eye SVG...

Writing hexagon emblem code...

Still building the arm chain...

I'm now checking the leg limb setup, verifying the reach distance against the hip joint, and adding the toe joint attachment point.

Next I'm working out the per-side leg geometry, pulling the knee, hip, and ankle points from the leg chain, then sweeping a tapered profile from thigh to shin for the boot and leg shape.

Adding thigh and shin armour plates...

Still building limb geometry...

Still placing boot geometry...

Adding a small teal heel glow box, then assigning boot colors—graphite body, white toe cap, teal accents—and confirming toe joint placement clears the floor properly. Then I'm planning torso ornamentation: small rivet spheres arranged in rings along the chest armor edges, merged onto the chest/hips bones.

I need to figure out where the rivets sit on the curved chest surface, so I'm setting up station data for the chest armor's width, height, and depth at different heights, then writing a helper to linearly interpolate between those stations and compute the front/back z-position of the ellipse at any given x and y, which I'll use to place rivets correctly against the armor surface.

Rather than scattering rivets everywhere, I'm planning more deliberate panel details: a chest decal, a glowing sternum strip, vent slits across the lower ribs, and teal glow lines on the side torso panels. I want to maximize visual richness with side panels, rivets, collars, and trim details, so I'm now writing functions to generate rivet rows on the chest front and back.

Now I'm designing the backpack — positioning it on the chest joint behind the torso and armor layers with a white outer box, dark inset panels, glowing teal vials, steel top caps, and a grille decal plane for the back vents.

I'm also sketching cable tubes that sweep from the pack down toward the belt using a catmull-rom curve through hip-area points.

Now I'm planning a small medical pouch on the right hip belt, a box shape with a white body and teal cross decal, positioning it alongside the hip plates.

Adding the right-side gear next: small teal-glow syringe cylinders stacked on the belt, skipping the thigh holster, and now working out shoulder pauldrons and upper-arm armor plating as a cylindrical wrap around the bicep.

Still writing armor rods...

I'm working out the radii tapering along the arm chain and bracer coverage, then moving on to the left cyborg arm: placing a steel shoulder ball joint and starting the upper arm rod from shoulder to elbow with its own tapered radius profile.

Now I'm adding steel collar rings around the arm joints, plus thin piston rods offset front and back of the limb, with a glowing teal conduit tube running alongside them.

For the elbow, I'm placing a metal ball joint bound to the elbow bone, then building the forearm as a hexagonal rod tapering from elbow to wrist, with white armor plates layered on top and the outer surface.

Now I'm working through adding a circuit decal to the forearm, figuring out the correct orientation vector so the pattern aligns vertically along the limb's natural axis rather than world up.

I decide the circuit's square, directionless pattern makes roll orientation irrelevant, so I move on. For the cyborg hand, I'm planning a metal palm box with chain-link finger sweeps and glowing joint rings at the tips.

I also need to resolve skin continuity: full-coverage sleeves and gloves mean only face and neck show skin, so I'll add a glowing seam-ring where the cyborg shoulder meets the torso. For a medic aesthetic, I'm considering adding a short tabard-style cape panel hanging from the belt, white with teal trim, to echo that Mercy-like silhouette.

Writing tabard geometry...

Finishing the swallowtail polygon points and typing it as an OutlinePoint array, then planning a thinner secondary extrude for the teal border panel using surface paint coordinates.

Instead of computing per-pixel distance for a border, I'll just layer two extrudes: a bigger teal panel behind and a smaller white panel in front, offset in z so the border peeks out from the front-facing side on the tabard, and the mirrored arrangement on the back tail.

Now I'm defining the staff joint attached to the wrist and setting up lathe profiles for its parts, starting with the foot — building a closed polygon of radius/height points around the staff's axis.

Next I'm detailing the lower shaft, grip, and ring grooves as rods with specific radii and tones.

Still designing the staff geometry...

Adding halo rings around the orb...

Finishing the feather outline for the angel fins, then adding a smaller teal glow extrude nested inside it for an inner light effect.

Checking the staff's top extent against the head height to make sure nothing clips, which looks fine. I'm now setting up the staff bone and finger bone naming for the right hand, making sure the names follow valid identifier rules with underscores allowed.
